# Ground Reaction Breakdown

## Status

Evidence class: derived, provisional. This chapter records the ground-reaction
calculation delivered by GCV-1 (#11707) so it can be inventoried. It is not
approved: the registry blocker `UP-D1-ground-reaction-breakdown-inventory`
stays open until UP-D1 inventories the pathway and a human reviews it.

## Purpose

Reduce the contact forces between each foot and the ground to the quantities
shown by every engine and display surface: per-foot force, centre of pressure
(CoP), free moment, the net (both-feet) wrench with its own CoP and free moment,
and the moments of each foot and of the net wrench about the whole-body centre
of mass (CoM).

## Conventions

- World frame, Z up, ground plane $z = z_g$ (default $z_g = 0$).
- SI units: force in N, position in m, moment in N·m, time in s.
- Sign: the force is exerted **by the ground on the foot** (on the body).
- Inputs per foot $f$: contact forces $F_i$ at points $p_i$, with optional
  contact torques $\tau_i$, all finite and in the world frame. A foot may have
  no contacts.
- The CoM position $c$ is a finite world 3-vector supplied by the caller.

## Equations

1. Foot resultant about the world origin $O$:
   $$F_f = \sum_i F_i, \qquad M_{O,f} = \sum_i \left(p_i \times F_i + \tau_i\right)$$
2. CoP of a resultant $(F, M_O)$ on the ground plane, defined only when
   $F_z \ge F_{z,\min}$ with $F_{z,\min} = 10$ N (`COP_MIN_FZ_N`):
   $$x_{cop} = \frac{z_g F_x - M_{O,y}}{F_z}, \qquad
     y_{cop} = \frac{M_{O,x} + z_g F_y}{F_z}, \qquad z_{cop} = z_g$$
3. Free moment about the CoP, reported as a vertical vector:
   $$T_z = M_{O,z} - \left(x_{cop} F_y - y_{cop} F_x\right)$$
4. Net wrench: $F_{net} = \sum_f F_f$ and $M_{O,net} = \sum_f M_{O,f}$; the net
   CoP and net free moment apply equations 2 and 3 to the net wrench. The net
   free moment is in general not $\sum_f T_{z,f}$: each foot's free moment is
   about its own CoP, and the shear forces acting at offset CoPs contribute a
   vertical moment to the net. The two agree when the foot CoPs coincide.
5. Moment about the CoM (full wrench):
   $$M_{c,f} = M_{O,f} - c \times F_f$$
   which equals $(cop_f - c) \times F_f + T_{z,f}\,\hat z$ when the CoP exists.
   The force-only term $(cop_f - c) \times F_f$ is reported separately.
   $M_{c,net} = \sum_f M_{c,f}$ exactly.

## Unavailable Values

Below the vertical-force threshold, or with no loaded contact, the CoP, the free
moment and the force-only CoM moment are unavailable (`None` in a breakdown,
NaN in a series, `null` over the API). They are never reported as zero. A foot
with no contact reports zero force and `in_contact = False`. Vertical load
share, used by the plots, is unavailable while the feet together carry less
than the same 10 N.

## Implementation

| Symbol | Location |
| --- | --- |
| `foot_reaction`, `analyze_ground_reaction`, `GroundReactionBreakdown` | `src/shared/python/biomechanics/ground_reaction.py` |
| `GroundReactionSeries` (stacked breakdowns, NaN for unavailable) | `src/shared/python/biomechanics/ground_reaction.py` |
| `to_overlay_wrenches` (overlay labels `contact:grf_*`, `contact:free_moment_*`, `contact:moment_com_*`) | `src/shared/python/biomechanics/ground_reaction.py` |

The module is pure numpy with no engine imports. Engines supply the contact
forces and points; the per-engine adapters are outside this chapter.

## Tests and Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/biomechanics/test_ground_reaction.py -q
```

These tests check the algebra against hand-computed wrenches and the stated
invariants (net CoM moment equals the sum of the feet; unavailable values below
the threshold). They do not check any engine's contact model.

## Assumptions and Limitations

- Flat, horizontal ground at a known height; no slope or compliance is modelled
  here.
- The 10 N threshold is a numerical guard against dividing by a small vertical
  force, not a physiological or instrument threshold.
- Results are only as valid as the contact forces each engine supplies.
  Software outputs of a contact model are not force-plate measurements, and no
  comparison with measured force-plate data has been made for this pathway.
- No uncertainty or tolerance against an external reference has been
  established; none is claimed.
